title: openingScene
body:
<< leftPlayer>> 
Sacrefice Dialogue
Good morning, Ms. Kitty
<< rightSpeaker>> 
Meow!
<< leftPlayer>> 
Still no sign of my aunt. Or anyone who will adopt you.
<< rightSpeaker>> 
Mrrp?
<< leftPlayer>> 
“Don’t worry, you still got me for another 4 days, until I begin my job as a
<< leftRepeater>> 
*sigh* storage levitation witch. 5 years of witch school and I’m cheaper than a forklift.”
<< leftNarrator>> 
[b]There is a knock on the door.[/b]
<< leftPlayer>> 
“Oh, maybe they’re here for you, Ms. Kitty!”
<< leftRepeater>> 
“Fiddlesticks, where did my aunt put the keys?”
<< leftRepeater>> 
“I don’t have time for this, I’ll just use what’s around me.
<< leftRepeater>> 
Surely there’s a lockpick potion in her witch’s book.” 
<< leftRepeater>> 
“I can switch between the storefront and the lab by clicking the arrow in the corner.”
<<scene1>>

title: openingDoorAndMeetingPrince
body:
<< leftPlayer>>
...
There, now it should be open! 
<< leftPlayer>> 
Good morning, are you here about the cat?
<< leftNarrator>> 
[b]A man walks in with a cape tightly held around him and the hood over his head, [/b]
<< leftNarrator>> 
[b]despite it being a warm and sunny day outside. [/b]
<< leftNarrator>> 
[b]He looks in every direction before walking in.[/b]
<< leftPlayer>> 
May I ask your name?
<<  actorSwitchRightPrinceHooded>>
<< rightSpeaker>>
Depends. Can you keep a secret?
<< leftPlayer>> 
Please leave.
<< rightSpeaker>> 
I’m just a friendly peasant, wishing to do business!
<< leftPlayer>>
Leave before I turn you into a toad.
<< rightSpeaker>>
That’s not the threat you think it is.
<<leftNarrator>>
[b]You ready your wand, and the mysterious man reveals himself.[/b]
<< actorSwitchRightPrinceNormal>> 
<< rightSpeaker>>
For as the prince of this land, a kiss from a beautiful maiden would transform me back!
<< leftPlayer>> 
...
<< rightSpeaker>>
...
<< leftNarrator>> 
[b]You lift a coin to compare them.[/b]
<< leftPlayer>> 
Your highness.
<< rightSpeaker>> 
No need to apologize.
<< leftPlayer>> 
Surely you have capable alchemists at the castle?
<< leftNarrator>> 
[b]His royal facade breaks into tears.[/b]
<< rightSpeaker>> 
Who do you think FAILED me? 
<< rightRepeater>> 
I’ve made them work on this for weeks, and now they’re no longer answering my summons!
<< leftSpeaker>> 
Your highness, I don’t even work here! 
I’ve barely finished witch school.
<< rightSpeaker>> 
You’re my only hope!!
<< leftSpeaker>>
I’m sorry, I-
Actually, I did just run out of catfood money.
<< rightSpeaker>> 
Meow
<< leftSpeaker>> 
Alright, just… tell me what you need and I’ll see what I can do.
First, I need more details. 
I can click on any character to ask them questions.
<<princeInstruction>> 
<< close>> 
PH

title: completePotionOfIlllumination
body:
<< rightNarrator>> 
The potion shines brightly.
<< actorSwitchRightPrinceNormal>> 
<< rightSpeaker>> 
Is this it?
<<leftPlayer>> 
Yes. Just make sure to-
<< rightNarrator>> 
The doorbell rings and a goblin walks in. 
<< rightNarrator>> 
She is dragging a sword along the floor that is way too big for her.
<< leftPlayer>> 
I forgot to lock the door…
<< actorSwitchRightGoblin>> 
<< actorSwitchLeftPrinceNormal>> 
<< rightSpeaker>> 
Oh, you’re open again! Perfect, I need a potion that-
<< leftSpeaker>> 
AHEM.
<< rightNarrator>> 
[b]The goblin looks at him for a moment, and then at you.[/b]
<< rightSpeaker>>
What’s his problem?
<< leftPlayer>>
You’re cutting in line. 
<< leftPlayer>> 
But more importantly, we’re not actually op-
<< rightSpeaker>> 
Oh, my bad, blondie.
<< leftPlayer>> 
*sigh*
<< leftSpeaker>> 
Little goblin, you are to show proper manners for someone of my status!
<< rightSpeaker>> 
I don’t know who you are, hotshot.
<< leftSpeaker>> 
Surely, you recognize me. You must!
<< rightSpeaker>> 
You must mistake me for some other goblin.
<<leftSpeaker>>
I’m the prince of this land!
<<rightNarrator>> 
[b]The goblin studies him, not really believing it.[/b]
<< leftSpeaker>> 
Please, just look at the coin you’re holding.
<< rightNarrator>> 
[b]She raises the coin up, comparing them.[/b]
<<rightSpeaker>> 
Oh yeah! I pay taxes to you!
<< leftSpeaker>> 
Finally!
<< rightSpeaker>> 
So what kind of work brings you here, then?
<< leftSpeaker>> 
Pardon?
<< rightSpeaker>> 
I’m paying you, aren’t I? What princely business is it spent on for the good of the kingdom?
<< leftSpeaker>> 
Can’t you tell? My golden locks, of course! A prince has to look fabulous!
<< rightNarrator>> 
The goblin is looks very unimpressed.
<< rightSpeaker>> 
Uh-huh.
<< leftSpeaker>> 
You'll see. Just as soon as I use this potion!
<< actorSwitchLeftNothing>> 
<< leftPlayer>> 
Wait, you really should put on-
<< leftNarrator>> 
Too late.
<< leftSpeaker>> 
- gloves....
<< leftNarrator>> 
The prince puts some on his hands and then onto his hair, both starting to glow.
He looks at himself in the reflection of the bottle.
<<actorSwitchLeftPrinceShining>>
Fabulous! Glorious! Spectacular! 
I have never looked better! 
Masterful witch, my saviour, please accept my deepest gratitude!
<< leftPlayer>> 
It was nothing, your highness.
<< leftSpeaker>> 
Truly? Then we shall speak of it no further.
Off to my adoring subjects!
<< rightNarrator>> 
The prince is about to run out the door, when his coat is held back by the goblin.
<< rightSpeaker>> 
Wait.
<< leftSpeaker>> 
Whatever is the matter?
<<rightSpeaker>>
Aren’t you forgetting something, little prince?
<< leftSpeaker>> 
...
Oh, of course!
Make me 2 more to bring with me!
<< rightSpeaker>> 
You forgot to pay!
<< leftSpeaker>> 
...Pardon?
<< rightSpeaker>> 
These shiny coins you compare yourself to, you have to give them to the potionmaker!
<< leftSpeaker>> 
... 
<< rightNarrator>> 
He’s got that nervous look again.
<< leftSpeaker>> 
It’s always the, uh, chauffeur that pays for me.
<< leftPlayer>> 
You didn’t bring ANY money?
<< rightNarrator>> 
You pull the potion back.
<< leftSpeaker>> 
No, please, I’ll do anything!
<< leftSpeaker>> 
I swear to the old oak and everything green, I’ll-!
<< rightNarrator>> 
The goblin’s expression suddenly changes from angry to mischievous.
<< rightSpeaker>> 
Actually, let’s turn this into a learning opportunity. 
Let me show you how things are done here in the “lower classes”, little prince.
I'll pay.
<< rightNarrator>> 
The goblin shows him 4 golden coins in her hand.
<< leftSpeaker>> 
You will? My hair is saved-
<< rightSpeaker>> 
IN RETURN for some honest, blue-collar work!
<< leftSpeaker>> 
My collar is white.
<< rightSpeaker>> 
Polish my sword, squire!
<< rightNarrator>> 
She drops her sword in the prince’s hands, and both fall to the floor with his hands stuck under it.
<<leftSpeaker>>
My nails! Why would you need such a heavy sword with your stature.
<< rightSpeaker>> 
Less whining, more shining! Take this wax and cloth, and rub it over the sword.
<< rightNarrator>> 
The prince looks like he’s about to cry.
<<leftSpeaker>>
For the good of the kingdom, I must!
<< goblinInstruction>> 
<<close>> 
...

title: goblinSoloBeforePotionMaking
body:
<< actorSwitchRightGoblin>> 
My turn.
<< leftPlayer>> 
I tried to tell you, we're not actually open!
<< rightSpeaker>> 
I’ll respect it if you say so, but it’s a reeeeally simple potion. 
Pretty please?
<< leftPlayer>> 
...I would like to have some human-food money too.
<< rightSpeaker>> 
I knew you were cool!
<< leftPlayer>> 
What can I do for you?
<< rightSpeaker>> 
Make the potion from “The Tale of the Mighty Draught”!
<< leftPlayer>> 
The bedtime story??
<< rightSpeaker>> 
Yes! 
The folks at the adventurer’s guild aren’t taking me seriously, saying my sword is too big for me.
<< leftPlayer>> 
Right.
<< rightSpeaker>> 
That’s bollocks, of course.
But with a strength potion, I could throw them around a lil bit, making them regret underestimating me!
<< leftPlayer>> 
I’m not making potions for violence.
<< rightSpeaker>> 
Alright, I hear you, I promise to only challenge them to arm wrestling.
Here’s the potion instructions.
<< leftNarrator>> 
The “instructions” are a copy of the popular bedtime story, hastily scribbled on a used napkin.
<< leftPlayer>> 
...I’ll see what I can do. I’m sure there’s a strength potion I can use in the witch’s book instead.
<< close>> 
PH

title: goblinStrengthPotionComplete
body:
<<actorSwitchRightGoblin>>
This is it!
<< leftPlayer>> 
You haven’t even tried it yet.
<< rightSpeaker>> 
I don’t need to, I saw you make it just like the story. This is it!
<< leftNarrator>> 
She takes a swig of the strength potion.
<< rightSpeaker>> 
YES. I feel the strength rushing through me, I can do anything!
<< leftNarrator>> 
She takes the sword from the prince’s hand, holding it up in the air like it weighs nothing.
<< rightSpeaker>> 
Thank you, potion witch!
<< leftPlayer>> 
You know, there’s a moral to the story.
About the nail’s contribution specifically.
<< rightSpeaker>> 
I know the moral! All 4 friends had to work together and use their differences to make something great!
<< leftPlayer>> 
*chuckle* I like that interpretation. I hope the potion serves you well.
<< rightSpeaker>> 
Speaking of friends, come over here, little prince.
<< actorSwitchLeftPrinceShining>> 
Absolutely dreadful. My poor, poor nails…
<< rightSpeaker>> 
You did well today! Here’s your payment, the price of a potion.
<< leftNarrator>> 
She puts 4 gold coins on the table. The prince looks exhausted, but proud of himself.
…until the goblin takes a coin away.
<<rightSpeaker>> 
Aaaand that’s the 25 percent tax paid to the royals.
<< leftNarrator>> 
The prince looks devastated.
<< rightSpeaker>> 
Hahaha, just kidding! 
<<leftSpeaker>>
Toying with my delicate heart…
I’ll return with the proper currency next time.
<< rightSpeaker>> 
You’re alright, little prince. Let’s go to the tavern!
<< leftSpeaker>> 
The tavern?
<< rightSpeaker>> 
It’s the best part of any workday! 
We sit together for a meal and toast to a job well done!
It’s right across the street!
<< leftNarrator>> 
The prince looks appalled.
<< leftSpeaker>> 
You can’t possibly mean… there? 
Where the floors are dirty from spilled beer and soiled boots?
With those foul-mouthed ruffians?
<< rightSpeaker>> 
With any luck it is! They know how to party!
<<leftSpeaker>>
Well, I’d never…!
<< leftNarrator>> 
He turns his head away, hiding a slight blush
<<leftSpeaker>>
I…
I shouldn’t squander such a… learning opportunity, as you called it. 
I shall accompany you to this… tavern.
<< rightSpeaker>> 
That’s the spirit!
<<leftNarrator>>
The goblin slaps him on the back, and they leave together.
<<actorSwitchLeftNothing>>
<< actorSwitchRightNothing>>
<< leftNarrator>> 
The sun has set and you take a moment to relax.
<< leftPlayer>> 
Phew, that’s enough for one day. 
It’s not what I planned, but…
<< rightSpeaker>> 
Meow!
<< leftPlayer>> 
I agree. I’m happy I got to help them.
<< close>> 
PH
